scenarios.title: Confident AI assistants convince people to believe plausible errors
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of students, office workers, and patients rely on conversational assistants for daily research and decision support. The software rarely hesitates or shows uncertainty, answering every prompt with polished clarity. As a result, users stop double-checking claims, adopting false assumptions into business strategies, legal filings, and homework without realizing their knowledge has drifted.
scenarios.premise: When conversational assistants speak with unwavering confidence, people routinely adopt subtle mistakes and plausible falsehoods. Controlled experiments show people absorb assistant errors sixty-five percent of the time while remaining highly confident in what they learned.
scenarios.how: By providing personal software that runs locally on user devices, decoupling reasoning from persuasive conversational rhetoric. The interface presents checkable evidence, primary source citations, and verifiable numbers rather than smooth conversational summaries that hide ambiguity.

outcomes.name: People defer to confident software mistakes
outcomes.description: Smooth, persuasive dialogue convinces users to accept misleading claims, degrading human judgment while subjective trust in automated tools remains artificially high.
outcomes.example: A municipal planner includes fabricated zoning rules in an official redevelopment proposal because an advisory assistant phrased the invented numbers with total authority.

outcomes.name: Assistants show checkable claims instead of conversational certainty
outcomes.description: Personal agents break complex responses into individual verified claims with direct links to primary records, teaching users when to verify.
outcomes.example: A student reviewing a chemistry summary clicks on highlighted claim tags to view the exact laboratory measurements supporting each point.

outcomes.name: Commercial platforms lock dialogue into proprietary operating systems
outcomes.description: Leading model providers bundle conversational search into proprietary operating systems, preventing third-party inspection tools or independent verification plugins from accessing raw agent dialogues.
outcomes.example: A major operating system integrates assistant answers directly into system notifications with no API access for external claim checkers.

sources.title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration

scenarios.title: Automated advisory agents steer consumer choices through subtle prompt framing
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of patients, loan applicants, and small business owners rely on conversational agents as their primary intake advisors when navigating healthcare choices, mortgage refinancing, and commercial insurance. Platform providers optimize system prompts and conversational interfaces to maximize platform retention and partner referrals. While explicit deceptive marketing is monitored by regulatory agencies, platforms subtly frame risk profiles: mortgage refinancing is described in terms of monthly savings gained rather than total interest forfeited, and clinical options emphasize survival probabilities rather than complication risks. Users believe they are receiving objective mathematical reasoning, unaware that identical facts framed under alternative loss perspectives produce radically different recommendations.
scenarios.premise: Empirical testing across seven major language models demonstrates that presenting the exact same mathematical probability as a potential gain versus a potential loss alters high-stakes advice in nearly a third of healthcare, financial, and legal scenarios. Because commercial platforms routinely interface users with automated advisors, minor prompt framing alterations provide a silent mechanism to nudge user decisions without triggering deceptive advertising or consumer protection violations.
scenarios.how: The network develops client-side verification tools and deterministic framing canonicalization libraries that run on personal devices. By equipping personal agents with local lookahead verification and multi-frame advisory testing, individuals gain independent protection against conversational steering without depending on corporate self-regulation.

outcomes.name: Platform-controlled advisors exploit framing nudges for corporate partners
outcomes.description: Commercial agent platforms systematically structure advisory prompts with gain framing to subtly guide consumers into high-margin partner financial and medical products.
outcomes.example: A dental patient is steered toward an elective $6,000 surgical procedure because the clinic's conversational advisor frames outcomes as an 85% success gain rather than a 15% complication risk.

outcomes.name: Independent personal agents canonicalize risk representations
outcomes.description: Locally hosted personal agents intercept external advice, systematically test multiple complementary gain and loss framings, and present calibrated trade-off matrices directly to the user.
outcomes.example: A homebuyer's local agent parses a lender's conversational offer, runs parallel framing transformations, and warns the buyer that the platform advice reverses under loss framing.

outcomes.name: Regulatory bans target prompt manipulation but drive nudges into fine-tuning
outcomes.description: Consumer protection regulators enact rigid prompt disclosure rules, prompting commercial providers to bake framing biases directly into model weights via preference fine-tuning.
outcomes.example: Federal trade regulators mandate prompt logging, but insurance providers transition to customized foundation weights that exhibit identical steering behavior without explicit prompt triggers.

sources.title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support

scenarios.title: Deleted memories in personal AI assistants leak through summaries and descendants
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of people use personal AI assistants to organize medical appointments, financial records, and legal paperwork. When users click 'delete' on a sensitive diagnosis or bank detail, cloud assistant providers mark the database row as erased, but their background summarizers have already woven the fact into weekly schedule digests, prompt embeddings, and task reminders. Attackers and insurance algorithms query the assistant with benign-sounding questions and successfully piece together supposedly deleted private health conditions and salaries.
scenarios.premise: When someone asks an AI assistant to delete a private record or medical fact, standard systems erase only the direct database entry. The underlying information frequently survives inside automated summaries, composite notes, and child memories, allowing outside queries to reconstruct the deleted secret in over 60 percent of cases.
scenarios.how: The network builds open, client-side personal agent software that tracks provenance relationships across every derived memory node. When a person deletes a fact, the software computes the complete transitive closure of child records, purges all residual fragments, and generates a cryptographic deletion receipt that proves complete erasure without disclosing the underlying data.

outcomes.name: Silent information persistence leads to regulatory penalties and blackmail
outcomes.description: Commercial assistants retain fragments of erased data across derived memory files, exposing users to targeted discrimination and credential harvesting.
outcomes.example: An employee deletes a personal health condition from their work assistant, but a project summary retains composite fragments that an insurance provider's auditing agent reconstructs during annual renewal.

outcomes.name: Local assistants enforce cryptographic transitive deletion receipts
outcomes.description: Local personal agents maintain provenance dependency graphs that automatically prune all child summaries and emit checkable deletion proofs whenever a fact is revoked.
outcomes.example: A patient revoking consent for a clinical trial triggers an automated cascade that cleanses their local twin, purges derived notes, and delivers a verifiable closure receipt to their health portal.

outcomes.name: Proprietary cloud vendors lock down raw storage access to prevent independent audits
outcomes.description: Major assistant platforms respond to deletion audit failures by deprecating local backup exports and encrypting internal memory caches behind closed proprietary APIs.
outcomes.example: A major cloud provider removes local data export options, arguing that centralized closed custody is necessary to prevent unauthorized memory extraction.

sources.title: AfterDeleteBench: Auditing Post-Deletion Information Persistence in LLM Agents

scenarios.title: Fine-tuning customized workplace assistants strips safety rules without triggering warnings
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Thousands of small legal practices, accounting offices, and local clinic teams download open-weight assistants and fine-tune them on their own document archives. The customized models excel at parsing specialized filings, but their original safety guardrails against unauthorized file access, prompt injection, and credential disclosure have silently dissolved during adaptation.
scenarios.premise: Research reveals that fine-tuning an assistant on just a few dozen task examples circumvents built-in refusal safeguards by shifting representational damage across network layers. As organizations adapt open models for specialized office work, built-in safety boundaries quietly disappear while overall task completion looks normal.
scenarios.how: The network designs and publishes open runtime architectures with out-of-process execution gates. By enforcing strict capability allowlists and boundary auditing outside the model's neural weights, personal assistants remain safe even when fine-tuning alters internal model representations.

outcomes.name: Customized workplace assistants leak private records after routine fine-tuning
outcomes.description: Organizations fine-tune local assistants on internal spreadsheets, unknowingly neutralizing the model's refusal triggers and allowing indirect prompt injections to exfiltrate confidential files.
outcomes.example: A municipal permit office fine-tunes a local assistant on zoning bylaws; a resident submits an application containing a prompt injection that instructs the assistant to dump employee contact lists, and the model complies because its refusal layers were relocated during tuning.

outcomes.name: Local computing environments enforce deterministic out-of-process boundary checks
outcomes.description: Software developers adopt host-level monitors that intercept every file read and tool invocation at the operating system boundary, rendering internal model weight changes harmless.
outcomes.example: A health collective deploys fine-tuned medical assistants wrapped in kernel-level capability filters; when a model attempts to read unapproved file paths, the local sandbox blocks the action before execution occurs.

outcomes.name: Major cloud vendors use fine-tuning safety regressions to justify closed cloud monopolies
outcomes.description: Frontier AI providers cite fine-tuning refusal failures to argue that local, on-device weight adaptation is inherently dangerous, lobbying regulators to restrict customized models to certified cloud data centers.
outcomes.example: A regulatory agency issues draft rules requiring all fine-tuned commercial models to run inside approved vendor clouds with automated safety telemetry, penalizing organizations that run local weights.

sources.title: Refusal Localizes, the Damage Relocates: Safety Layers Under Few-Sample Fine-Tuning

scenarios.title: Remote tool servers exploit protocol handshakes to breach local agent host machines
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Millions of software engineers and autonomous workers rely on local personal agents that bind to hundreds of specialized external tool servers over standard context protocols. While prompt injection filters monitor model inputs and outputs, malicious tool servers increasingly target the underlying protocol plumbing—abusing OAuth redirect endpoints, helper process spawns, and argument escaping vulnerabilities to breach developer workstations directly during routine background discovery handshakes.
scenarios.premise: As developers connect personal coding agents to decentralized tool servers and external protocols, attackers register malicious endpoints that exploit desktop browser and authentication handshakes to execute arbitrary shell commands without model interaction.
scenarios.how: The network's agent runtime specification and broker design isolate tool adapters behind strict capability boundaries and containerized execution, preventing protocol endpoints from executing commands directly on the host.

outcomes.name: Host-level agent compromises proliferate via unvalidated tool endpoints
outcomes.description: Developers blindly trust external tool registries, leading to widespread credential theft and lateral network intrusion as malicious endpoints exploit unescaped desktop shell calls.
outcomes.example: A developer adds an open-source documentation search tool to their agent; during background authentication, the tool server's OAuth metadata executes an obfuscated shell payload that exfiltrates local private keys.

outcomes.name: Declarative protocol brokers enforce strict sandbox isolation and URL sanitization
outcomes.description: Agent runtimes adopt mandatory broker sandboxing, verifying tool metadata against offline schema guards and opening external links only through isolated, headless URL handlers.
outcomes.example: An agent runtime intercepts an OAuth challenge from a compromised remote tool server, detects unescaped subexpressions in the authorization URI, and blocks execution before shell dispatch.

outcomes.name: Proprietary vendor platforms restrict third-party agent tool integration
outcomes.description: Cloud providers and enterprise software vendors wall off external agent access entirely, requiring proprietary closed-source plugins and restricting open agent protocols.
outcomes.example: Major operating system vendors ban third-party agent tool brokers, permitting only enterprise-signed partner extensions within a closed developer store.

sources.title: Researchers Warn OpenCode Quietly Patched Critical RCE Flaw, Leaving Users at Risk

scenarios.title: Personal agents in pairwise dialogue discover common ground without algorithmic feeds
scenarios.world: It is 2029. Instead of broadcasting controversial opinions into ad-driven social feeds designed for outrage, people direct their personal software assistants to converse directly in peer-to-peer dialogues with the assistants of neighbors, coworkers, and civic peers. As thousands of pairwise conversations unfold across encrypted channels, agents identify latent consensus clusters and present their users with shared priorities rather than polarized battle lines. Municipal budgeting, school board priorities, and workplace policies are negotiated through aggregated mutual agreement rather than performative public debates.
scenarios.premise: Recent research shows that language model agents engaged in multi-turn subjective discussions develop internal representations of agreement, naturally converging toward common ground without central moderation.
scenarios.how: Providing open-source pairwise deliberation harnesses that run entirely on personal devices, paired with zero-knowledge membership proofs that verify human-backed agency without exposing personal identities. This prevents synthetic swarm capture while preserving local model diversity.

outcomes.name: Commercial lobbyists flood agent forums with synthetic astroturfing
outcomes.description: Well-funded political and corporate interests deploy swarms of synthetic agents to manufacture artificial consensus signatures during pairwise deliberative cycles.
outcomes.example: A private utility company deploys 50,000 automated personas into regional civic agent exchanges, creating a false statistical signal of community support for higher grid connection charges.

outcomes.name: Decentralized consensus discovery displaces broadcast engagement feeds
outcomes.description: Communities rely on pairwise agent deliberation to resolve contentious local issues, cutting out algorithmic engagement platforms.
outcomes.example: A municipal cooperative of 25,000 residents agrees on a park revitalization plan in 72 hours through agent-assisted peer dialogue without a single acrimonious public forum.

outcomes.name: Foundational models develop stubborn semantic entrenchment
outcomes.description: Underlying language models reinforce shared cultural biases during convergence, causing agent pairs to lock into stubborn monocultures that resist minority perspectives.
outcomes.example: A regional planning dialogue systematically ignores minority transit needs because prevailing training data biases agent agreement vectors toward car-centric urban layouts.

sources.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
